title: City of London Police
summary: This document provides a comprehensive overview of the City of London Police, the territorial police force responsible for law enforcement within the City of London, England. The document begins by describing the force's role as the national lead police force for fraud, its distinction from the Metropolitan Police, its workforce statistics, and its status as the smallest territorial police force in England and Wales. It then traces the force's history from its origins in 1832 through the City of London Police Act 1839, covering significant events including officer deaths in the line of duty, involvement in the Jack the Ripper investigation, Olympic gold medals in tug of war, IRA bombings in the 1990s and the establishment of the "ring of steel," and its 2014 designation as the lead force for fraud operating the National Fraud Intelligence Bureau and Report Fraud service. The document includes a chronological list of police commissioners from 1839 to the present, details the force's organizational structure across five directorates (with emphasis on its economic crime expertise), and outlines the current leadership team. Additional sections cover the force's distinctive uniform featuring brass badges and red and white chequered bands, its equipment and vehicle fleet (including Taser usage statistics), its mounted unit, rank structure and insignia, workforce composition, and the Special Constabulary including its 2023 restructuring and list of chief officers. The document concludes by noting other limited policing bodies operated by the City of London Corporation that are separate from the police force.
